message.content: Fusion research has improved plasma diagnostics, creating methods now used for medical imaging, material inspection, and laboratory safety. Magnet development for fusion helped create stronger superconducting magnets that support medical scanners, particle accelerators, and transport systems. Fusion neutron experiments have trained engineers to model radiation damage, verify safeguards, and test materials for safer energy systems. Plasma tools developed for fusion also help control contamination in semiconductor fabs, sterilize equipment, and monitor atmospheric emissions. These iritic gains show that fusion science already produces useful technologies, even while commercial power remains a longer term goal.
